papers.title: Disen-Forcing: Disentangling Semantic Anchoring from Motion for Autoregressive Video Diffusion
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models (AR-VDMs) enable real-time, long-horizon video generation but degrade rapidly once the inference horizon outruns the training horizon, due to compounding exposure bias. To stabilize long rollouts, recent methods heuristically adopt frame sink, keeping initial frames as a persistent model context, inspired by attention sinks in LLMs. We revisit this design and find that the mechanism by which initial frames stabilize long-range consistency in AR-VDMs is not an LLM-style attention sink; instead, long-range consistency is anchored through a sparse subset of attention heads, while the majority of heads predominantly capture local temporal dynamics. This observation reveals an over-conditioning pathology in existing frame-sink strategies: by universally exposing every head to the pinned initial-frame context, the model becomes prone to collapsing motion toward the low-dynamic modes of the teacher during model distillation. We propose Disen-Forcing, a distillation-time plug-in for AR-VDMs that disentangles and reinforces this head specialization through disentangled context routing and motion-disentangling regularization. On long-horizon video generation benchmarks, Disen-Forcing simultaneously improves long-range consistency and motion dynamics of base AR-VDMs, a trade-off that sink-based methods fail to balance.
papers.summary_cn: Autoregressive video diffusion models (AR-VDMs) enable real-time, long-horizon video generation but degrade rapidly once the inference horizon outruns the training horizon, due to compounding exposure bias.
papers.contribution_cn: We propose Disen-Forcing, a distillation-time plug-in for AR-VDMs that disentangles and reinforces this head specialization through disentangled context routing and motion-disentangling regularization.

papers.title: History Forcing: Distilling History-Dependent Continuations for Long-Horizon Video World Models
papers.abstract: Few-step autoregressive video diffusion enables efficient generation, yet maintaining consistency over long rollouts remains challenging, especially when subjects or scenes reappear after going out of sight. Despite progress in fidelity and rollout robustness, existing distillation methods do not fully exploit richer historical information to constrain the student's current prediction. To address this gap, we introduce \textbf{History Forcing}, a unified on-policy distillation framework that strengthens historical supervision for few-step autoregressive video generators. The framework uses the residual between teacher predictions with and without informative historical context to decouple this supervision. Such a historical context can be obtained using earlier generated chunks with less accumulated drift or a fixed-view teacher rollout that keeps the scene visible while the student looks away. The residual is then weighted and added to the score or velocity prediction used for distillation, forming a corrected target. By aligning the student with this corrected target through distillation, History Forcing incorporates long-range historical constraints into autoregressive generation. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance among 1.3B models, with a VBench quality score of 85.07 for 15s video generation and a VBench-Long aggregate score of 79.82 for 60s generation. For out-of-sight world modeling, evaluations further demonstrate more plausible scene evolution and more consistent states when the camera returns, with Evolution Quality improving from 2.35 to 2.70 on PlayWorld and Object Consistency from 58.43 to 62.18 on MemoBench.
papers.summary_cn: 本文提出History Forcing，用于解决少步自回归视频扩散在长时间生成和视野外场景演化中的历史一致性问题。方法比较自回归教师在有、无额外历史信息时对同一噪声片段的预测，以提取历史残差，并将其加入双向教师的分数目标或EMA教师的速度目标，从而在保留视觉质量监督的同时强化长程历史约束。实验显示，该方法改善了15秒和60秒视频的主体、背景及运动一致性，也提升了摄像机离开后场景演化和返回时的物体状态一致性，同时训练开销仅小幅增加。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出History Forcing统一蒸馏框架，通过有历史与无历史教师预测之间的上下文残差，将历史监督与整体生成质量监督解耦，并可用于DMD和在线策略自蒸馏。 2. 针对长视频生成，使用同一学生滚动中的较早生成片段构造历史，减轻主体外观和场景布局的累积漂移。 3. 针对视野外世界建模，使用保持固定视角的教师滚动生成构造不可见期间的历史，监督场景演化及摄像机返回后的状态恢复。 4. 在1.3B模型上取得15秒VBench质量85.07和60秒VBench-Long聚合79.82；在PlayWorld和MemoBench上提升场景演化、主体身份和物体一致性。 5. 通过仅对一个随机片段施加历史监督，将相对DMD的每步训练时间和峰值显存增幅控制在2.31%和1.99%。
papers.relevance_cn: 与研究重点高度相关。该工作直接研究视频扩散、自回归生成、长视频生成和视频世界模型。其核心方法通过历史残差蒸馏增强长程一致性，适用于少步生成器，因而兼顾生成效率与长期稳定性；固定视角教师滚动还支持摄像机离开视野后的闭环场景模拟和状态演化。方法建立在DMD、在线策略蒸馏和速度目标之上，与实时生成、蒸馏和流式/因果生成密切相关，但论文未以缓存复用或稀疏注意力为主要技术贡献。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出，长视频实验仅使用1.3B规模的教师和学生模型，世界建模实验使用5B骨干网络。历史监督的有效性仍受底层模型捕捉时间动态能力的限制；在世界建模中，固定视角教师滚动生成的场景演化可能有限，从而削弱对视野外状态变化的监督。论文还指出需要进一步研究更大规模的教师和学生、更长上下文训练，以及物理上更合理的世界模型动态模拟。
papers.abstract_cn: 少步自回归视频扩散能够实现高效生成，但在长时间滚动生成中保持一致性仍然具有挑战性，尤其是当主体或场景离开视野后再次出现时。尽管视频保真度和滚动鲁棒性已有提升，现有蒸馏方法仍未充分利用更丰富的历史信息来约束学生模型当前的预测。为解决这一问题，我们提出 History Forcing，一种统一的在线策略蒸馏框架，用于强化少步自回归视频生成器中的历史监督。该框架利用教师模型在有信息历史上下文和无该上下文条件下预测结果之间的残差，将这种监督信号解耦出来。历史上下文可以通过累积漂移较小的早期生成片段获得，也可以通过固定视角的教师滚动生成获得；后者在学生模型转移视线时保持场景可见。随后，将该残差加权并加入蒸馏所使用的分数或速度预测中，从而形成修正后的目标。通过蒸馏使学生模型对齐这一修正目标，History Forcing 将长程历史约束融入自回归生成。在1.3B模型中，我们的方法取得了当前最优的性能：15秒视频生成的VBench质量得分为85.07，60秒生成的VBench-Long聚合得分为79.82。在视野外世界建模任务中，评估进一步表明，该方法能够产生更合理的场景演化，并在摄像机返回时保持更一致的状态；在PlayWorld上，Evolution Quality从2.35提升至2.70，在MemoBench上，Object Consistency从58.43提升至62.18。

papers.title: PrimeSim: A Generalist World Model Simulator from Large-Scale Cross-Embodiment Demonstrations
papers.abstract: A robot world model that serves as a simulator must do more than generate plausible videos: it must faithfully follow commanded actions, maintain consistency across camera views, and sustain coherent long-horizon rollouts. We present PrimeSim, an action-conditioned, multiview world model simulator that addresses these challenges through progressive midtraining and posttraining. Starting from a pretrained video generator, we midtrain on 30,110 hours of robot demonstrations spanning 22 platforms. To improve action following, we introduce a unified cross-embodiment action representation and frame-aligned dual-path conditioning to strengthen action-frame correspondence. To maintain multiview consistency, we develop view-aware interleaved attention with explicit camera identities, enabling cross-view information exchange while preserving view-specific representations. We further introduce a fast-video, slow-memory posttraining framework that transforms the bidirectional video generator into an efficient autoregressive simulator. By combining fast causal generation, self-rollout training, and hierarchical temporal memory, PrimeSim mitigates error accumulation from self-generated histories and supports coherent long-horizon simulation. PrimeSim runs at 10.1 FPS, remains stable over long-horizon rollouts on rigid and deformable manipulation tasks, and transfers to held-out platforms within 100 to 200 gradient steps where the pretrained backbone does not. Against five open-source action-conditioned world models it leads four of the five WorldSimProbe suites and posts the best overall EWMBench score, while fine-grained local calibration still trails the field; its rollouts are faithful enough to support GRPO-based policy optimization. We release the model weights, inference code, and training code.
papers.summary_cn: PrimeSim 将预训练视频生成器改造成面向机器人操作的动作条件、多视角、因果自回归世界模型模拟器。模型在 30,110 小时、22 个机器人平台的数据上训练，通过统一的 31 维跨具身动作表示、帧对齐双路径动作条件和带摄像机身份的交错注意力，实现动作跟随与多视角一致性。后期训练依次采用块因果建模、四步一致性蒸馏、自 rollout 分布匹配以及分层 KV 时间记忆，使模型能够以 10.1 FPS 进行最长约 105 秒的长时域模拟。实验显示，PrimeSim 在 WorldSimProbe 的五项测试中领先四项，EWMBench 总分为 6.09，并能较准确地预测策略成功率、支持在模型内部进行 GRPO 策略优化。模型对未见平台和场景具有一定迁移能力，但仍存在分辨率较低、局部动作校准不足以及尚未在真实硬件上验证闭环策略训练等问题。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出 PrimeSim，一种将通用视频生成器转化为动作条件、多视角、长时域机器人模拟器的渐进式训练框架。2. 构建涵盖 22 个机器人平台的 30,110 小时演示数据，并提出统一的跨具身动作表示和以窗口首帧为基准的相对动作块。3. 提出帧对齐双路径动作条件机制，将帧级动作注意力与动作-帧适配器结合，增强动作与生成运动之间的精确对应。4. 提出带显式摄像机身份的视角感知交错注意力，在跨视角交换信息的同时保留视角特定表示。5. 提出“快速视频、慢速记忆”的后期训练流程，结合块因果生成、四步一致性蒸馏、自 rollout 非对称分布匹配和分层时间记忆，降低推理成本并缓解长时域误差累积。6. 通过 WorldSimProbe、EWMBench、未见平台迁移和闭环策略实验验证模拟器的动作保真度、长时域稳定性与策略优化价值，并发布权重及代码。
papers.relevance_cn: 论文与研究重点高度相关。它直接研究动作条件视觉世界模型和闭环模拟：根据机器人动作预测多摄像机未来观测，并用世界模型自身生成的历史驱动后续 rollout。其块因果注意力、四步一致性蒸馏和自 rollout 训练对应因果、自回归、流式及实时视频生成；10.1 FPS 的推理速度面向控制环路。分层 KV-cache 将初始场景、稀疏长期历史和密集近期运动结合，直接涉及缓存复用与长视频生成。模型还通过在 PrimeSim 内进行 GRPO 训练并转移到 LIBERO 模拟器，展示了闭环策略优化和世界模型作为学习环境的用途。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出，PrimeSim 每个视角仅生成 192×256 分辨率，因此结论主要涉及模拟器保真度、动作实现和环境响应，而非高分辨率像素级真实感。迁移到新平台仍需要该平台数据上的 100 至 200 个梯度步，并非零样本迁移。大多数定量结果以及全部闭环策略训练和评估都来自 LIBERO 等模拟环境；真实机器人数据上的结果尚未证明其能够在真实硬件上承担策略改进所需的模拟器角色。WorldSimProbe 中 PrimeSim 的细粒度局部动作校准不如 LingBot-VA。EWMBench 结果主要来自训练分布内的 AgiBot World，且不同模型的推理分辨率、预测时域和去噪步数并未完全匹配；吞吐率比较也不是端到端控制环路测试。论文未明确说明在更复杂真实接触、长期真实部署和更长训练预算下的性能上限。
papers.abstract_cn: 作为模拟器使用的机器人世界模型不能只生成看似合理的视频：它还必须忠实执行指定动作、保持不同摄像机视角之间的一致性，并维持长时域 rollout 的连贯性。我们提出 PrimeSim，一种通过渐进式中期训练和后期训练解决这些挑战的动作条件多视角世界模型模拟器。PrimeSim 从预训练视频生成器出发，在涵盖 22 个平台的 30,110 小时机器人演示数据上进行中期训练。为改进行为跟随能力，我们提出统一的跨具身动作表示和帧对齐双路径条件机制，以增强动作与帧之间的对应关系。为保持多视角一致性，我们设计了带有显式摄像机身份的视角感知交错注意力，使不同视角能够交换信息，同时保留各视角特有的表示。我们进一步提出快速视频、慢速记忆的后期训练框架，将双向视频生成器转换为高效的自回归模拟器。该框架结合快速因果生成、自 rollout 训练和分层时间记忆，减轻自生成历史带来的误差累积，并支持连贯的长时域模拟。PrimeSim 的运行速度为 10.1 FPS，在刚性和可变形物体操作任务上能够进行稳定的长时域 rollout；在预训练骨干无法实现的情况下，它可在 100 至 200 个梯度步内迁移到未参与训练的平台。在与五个开源动作条件世界模型的比较中，PrimeSim 在五个 WorldSimProbe 套件中的四个取得领先，并获得 EWMBench 最高的总体分数；但其细粒度局部校准仍落后于最佳方法。其 rollout 的保真度足以支持基于 GRPO 的策略优化。我们发布模型权重、推理代码和训练代码。

papers.title: Learning-to-Memorize: Dynamic Context Management for Long-Horizon Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video generation has achieved impressive results on short clips, yet generating long videos remains challenging due to error accumulation over extended horizons, where each predicted frame depends on potentially imperfect previous frames. Existing approaches typically rely on static context management strategies, such as sliding-window caches that discard early frames or fixed sink frames that permanently preserve initial content. These designs either lose critical long-range context or anchor generation to outdated information, which can lead to degraded fidelity, motion stagnation, and reduced diversity. In this paper, we propose Learning to Memorize (L2M), a learned context memory management framework that dynamically retains, evicts, and evolves historical frames according to predicted importance. The framework consists of an importance prediction router that estimates the relevance of each historical frame, degradation-aware training that improves robustness to noisy or corrupted context, and a dynamic memory initialization and evolution mechanism that updates long-term memory using exponential moving average (EMA) importance scores. This allows high-quality frames to replace stale anchors and enables memory to adapt naturally to scene evolution. Trained with a teacher-student distillation objective and sparsity regularization, L2M makes efficient use of a fixed KV-cache budget while preserving the most informative contextual information. Extensive experiments demonstrate that L2M improves long-horizon video generation quality and temporal consistency over existing baselines, providing a learned strategy for context memory management in long autoregressive video generation.
papers.summary_cn: Autoregressive video generation has achieved impressive results on short clips, yet generating long videos remains challenging due to error accumulation over extended horizons, where each predicted frame depends on potentially imperfect previous frames.
papers.contribution_cn: In this paper, we propose Learning to Memorize (L2M), a learned context memory management framework that dynamically retains, evicts, and evolves historical frames according to predicted importance.

papers.title: Runway Characters: Serving a 57B Video Diffusion Transformer for Real-Time Conversation
papers.abstract: Conversational video characters must generate video as fast as it plays, for one user at a time: at 24 fps, a sustained 166.7 ms per four-frame chunk at batch size one, with only a few chunks of buffering. We describe the system behind Runway Characters, which serves a $\approx$57B-parameter autoregressive video diffusion transformer (four denoising passes per chunk) at 704$\times$1088 and 24 fps on four H100 GPUs with a voice agent in the loop. Each chunk takes 240 attention calls, each reading a 5,788-slot KV cache in which only 757 tokens are new, and 29% of the original step was whole-cache work repeated in every call. We move that work to write time (a ring cache, RoPE and FP8 quantization applied once per write, and a delta rotation when positions reset), fuse the tensor-parallel all-reduce into the FP8 GEMM with in-switch reduction, and give the decoder that turns latents into video frames its own GPU. Without the fused kernel, our optimizations cut the diffusion step from 240.9 to 159.3 ms (1.51$\times$, 24.5 fps sustained) with no detected degradation in lip-sync scores; the fused kernel, rolled back once in production and since re-enabled, reaches 147.4 ms (1.63$\times$, 43% of FP8 peak). In seven weeks of production the worker averaged above 23.5 fps in 99.5% of sessions that streamed for at least a second, and our pipeline takes 0.49 s of a 2.1 s median conversational turn. On the same GPUs, the two open-source real-time video systems we benchmarked, at four denoising passes, miss real time or add over a second of latency (one by estimate), at a third to half of our resolution.

papers.title: Future Representation Distillation for Imagination-free World Action Models
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) use the predictive knowledge of pretrained video diffusion models for robot control through future video prediction. However, iterative video denoising is costly, and inaccurate visual predictions can compromise action prediction. Our key idea is to make this predictive knowledge available through visual representations computed from the current observation, enabling action prediction without generating future videos. We introduce DreamFree, a WAM that repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a predictive visual encoder through representation distillation. The visual encoder learns to predict a frozen video diffusion model's representation using only the current observation. An action module is then trained to predict actions by extracting action-relevant information from the visual encoder. Across real-world and simulated tasks, DreamFree achieves higher success rates than state-of-the-art VLAs and WAMs, while performing real-time closed-loop control at 11Hz with a 14B video diffusion backbone. Experiments show that DreamFree can translate stronger video priors and additional video data into better robot control and enable learning new robot tasks from video demonstrations, including videos from a different embodiment, without action annotation for the new tasks.
papers.summary_cn: World Action Models (WAMs) use the predictive knowledge of pretrained video diffusion models for robot control through future video prediction.
papers.contribution_cn: We introduce DreamFree, a WAM that repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a predictive visual encoder through representation distillation.

papers.title: TouchéWorld tech report : Towards Online Unified Camera--Hand Exploration in Generative Worlds
papers.abstract: Recent video world models allow users to explore generated environments through camera navigation. Continuous hand motion provides a fine-grained action channel for interacting with the people and objects encountered during exploration. We present TouchéWorld, a framework that integrates gesture-driven interaction into a camera-controlled video world model. Given an initial image and a scene-description prompt, the model generates video conditioned on temporally aligned camera and hand controls. We construct joint camera--hand training data from heterogeneous egocentric videos through annotation completion, consistency-based filtering, and temporal alignment. Building on a pretrained camera-controlled world model, we combine spatial hand-skeleton conditioning with numerical hand-motion features through parameter-efficient adaptation. Causal adaptation and few-step distillation support chunk-level online generation, allowing users to update their controls based on generated visual feedback. We further introduce TouchéBench to evaluate hand-motion following, camera--hand coordination, online interaction, and object response. Together, these components establish a framework for studying continuous exploration and hand-driven interaction within generative worlds.
papers.summary_cn: Recent video world models allow users to explore generated environments through camera navigation.
papers.contribution_cn: We present TouchéWorld, a framework that integrates gesture-driven interaction into a camera-controlled video world model.

papers.title: When Does Latent Prediction Error Support Physical Surprise Claims in Video World Models?
papers.abstract: Prediction errors from video world models are often treated as physical surprise, but they can also reflect appearance, static content, motion, or ordinary prediction difficulty. We present an evaluation framework that separates what frozen representations contain, how they organize appearance and physical differences, and what changes a model's own prediction error. On IntPhys2, a benchmark of physically possible and impossible events, we compare representations from latent prediction, masked pixel reconstruction, and simple visual statistics. Appearance remains easy to decode, while V-JEPA2 exposes modest information about whether events are possible or impossible. Looking at the latent geometry, appearance changes become smaller compared with differences between videos, their directions line up more consistently across scenes, and their overlap with physical changes decreases in deeper layers. Across action-conditioned models, incorrect actions raise prediction error, while appearance changes also produce substantial responses. In Physion++ video clips, repeating a single frame can produce higher error than the original clip, while changing color throughout the clip can lower it. Using Kubric, a simulation and rendering framework, we find that impossible events can produce lower error than possible events. A fixed error threshold also incorrectly flags many possible events as impossible. A model can therefore represent physical information and respond to incorrect actions without its native prediction error reliably measuring physical surprise.

papers.title: ReactWorld: Structuring Interaction Responses for Embodied Video Generation
papers.abstract: Embodied video world models predict scene changes caused by robot actions, yet generated object responses may remain inconsistent with task intent and contact dynamics. Critical responses in embodied scenes often concentrate in local regions and specific time intervals. Inspired by chain-of-thought reasoning, we introduce ReactWorld, an embodied video generation model guided by structured interaction anticipation. In the generation backbone's feature space, an interaction response field predictor anticipates how the interaction will unfold, explicitly describing participant roles, future motion response intensity, and local motion changes. A response feedback adapter forms increments to object features from the difference between the object branch's outputs with predicted and zeroed local dynamics inputs. It also converts predicted displacements into positional biases for temporal attention. These two mechanisms guide object feature updates and information retrieval across frames, respectively. Through interaction anticipation and generative feedback, ReactWorld achieves an average score of 77.51 on RBench, outperforming PhysisForcing by 3.29 points with improvements in all nine categories. On EZS-Bench, it achieves a Domain score of 86.98 and an average score of 81.87.

papers.title: Hybrid Particle-Voxel Dynamics for Multimodal 3D World Simulation
papers.abstract: Predicting how the world evolves in response to robot actions is central to policy learning, evaluation, and planning. However, many action-conditioned world models predict future observations in 2D image or video space without explicitly modeling the underlying 3D scene, making spatial consistency across viewpoints and over long-horizon interactions challenging. We introduce 3D World Simulator, an action-conditioned multimodal world modeling framework that jointly predicts appearance, geometry, and tactile observations from a unified 3D representation. Our approach combines a hybrid particle-voxel autoencoder that compresses point clouds into compact 3D voxel latents with an action-conditioned latent dynamics model that predicts their evolution. The shared 3D representation supports geometrically consistent rendering from arbitrary viewpoints and flexible integration of spatially aligned tactile signals. Our experiments demonstrate interactive, long-horizon, multimodal prediction at 50 Hz. We then show how our model enables scalable data generation for policy training and evaluation using tactile and multi-view visual observations, including wrist-mounted and novel camera views. Furthermore, we scale our method to large datasets containing diverse objects and demonstrate model-based planning with unseen objects and robot configurations. Together, these results highlight the potential of hybrid particle-voxel dynamics as a foundation for multimodal 3D world simulation.
